body:
Every edit to the v0.8.0 cache read gate cold-rebuilds the whole corpus, because
cache **mechanism** code is folded into the **content** fingerprint. That is a
standing tax on precisely the code most likely to need fixing.

Found while landing #891/#892 (PR #893), where it shaped the design; filed
separately because the fix is a refactor of the repo's most delicate function.

## Measured

`_aggregate_wave_data` carries `@build_transform()` (`country.py:3472`), so its
nested `load_dataframe_with_dvc` closure is hashed **as source text**. Adding a
single no-op comment line inside that closure:

```
build_transforms_fingerprint('sample')   c4396fc77e404e38  ->  960b055cf10bf612
Country._table_cache_hash('Albania', 'household_roster')
                                      737448610a4ed243  ->  d2f75a257d3c584b
```

One comment. Every table in every country grades `stale`.

Attribution across the #891 change (measured by swapping each file
independently against HEAD):

| state | `btf` | Albania roster hash |
|---|---|---|
| HEAD | `c4396fc77e40` | `737448610a4e` |
| `local_tools.py` only (`to_parquet`) | **moved** | **moved** |
| both files | same as above | same as above |
| `country.py` only | *no movement of its own* | — |

## Why this is inconsistent with the existing design

`_build_registry._EXCLUDED_CALLABLES` already makes exactly this argument, in
its own comment:

> Cache/hash MECHANISM callables: they compute or compare the embedded cache
> hash and never touch DataFrame CONTENT. Excluded per-callable so folding them
> does not make the content fingerprint self-referential -- editing the cache
> layer would otherwise rebuild every cache.

`cache_freshness`, `read_parquet_cache_hash`, `stamp_parquet_hash`,
`Wave._input_hash` and `Country._table_cache_hash` are all excluded on that
reasoning. But the **gate that calls them** — the ~90-line v0.8.0 read block
inside `load_dataframe_with_dvc` — is not a callable, it is closure text inside
a tagged function, so it is hashed anyway. The exclusion is defeated by where
the code happens to live.

`to_parquet` is a separate case and its inclusion is deliberate and correct
(`_build_registry.py:112`: "it mutates content on write"). It is not what this
issue asks to change.

## Suggested fix

Extract the v0.8.0 read gate from the `load_dataframe_with_dvc` closure into a
method — `Country._read_l2_country_cache(method_name, cache_path, waves)`
returning the served frame or a sentinel — and add it to
`_EXCLUDED_CALLABLES` with the same justification as its neighbours. It reads
the parquet, compares hashes, checks coverage and filters; it determines no byte
of what a build writes.

Verify the same way the null-read audit's exclusion is verified: assert that
editing the extracted method moves no `build_transforms_fingerprint` value,
alongside `tests/test_build_transform_hash.py`'s existing pins. The extraction
itself invalidates once.

## Why now

The extraction costs one corpus invalidation whenever it lands. It is cheapest
while the corpus is already stale — **200 of 201 L2-country parquets measured
stale** during the #891 work, since v0.12.0 landed after the last re-warm, and
35 further commits have landed since. Doing it before the next re-warm makes it
free; doing it after means paying for a second one.

Ledger writeup: `.coder/ledger/891-wave-subset-cache.md` §9.

-- Sue

comments.body:
PR #1027 (`fix/908-920-read-gate`, `bb6c128a8`) resolves this issue (`Closes #908`, fires on release).

**Correction to the title/text:** a *comment* edit never moved the corpus. `_build_registry._norm` hashes `ast.dump` with docstrings stripped, and `ast.dump` drops comments; measured on base, appending a comment to `_aggregate_wave_data` left `build_transforms_fingerprint('sample')` unchanged, while appending a statement moved it. The defect is that any *logic* edit to the read gate moved every hash.

The same class of problem at the wave tier (`Wave.grab_data`, `run_make_target`, the `assume_cache_fresh` serve) is outside this issue and is split out as #1040.

title: Cache mechanism code is inside the content fingerprint: one comment in load_dataframe_with_dvc cold-rebuilds the corpus
